answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a bonded anchor: each new agent must lock a stake and pass blind peer review of its submitted work before it earns any weight. Graders see the artifact but not the identity, so a farm of clones costs one stake and one review cycle per head, and their shared phrasing stands out like a crack in a crystal. Reputation is plotted on a public atlas of verified tasks instead of wallet counts, which keeps duplicate identities visible and expensive.
